+# Old origin files (`https://dailygrind.example.com`)
+
+The Daily Grind installed web app is moving from `https://dailygrind.example.com`
+to `https://app.dailygrind.example.com`. The repo root is the new app; the files
+in this directory must be deployed to the **old** origin.
+
+| File | Served at | Purpose |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `.well-known/web-app-origin-association` | `https://dailygrind.example.com/.well-known/web-app-origin-association` | Authorizes the new origin to take over the installation. Serve as `application/json`. |
+| `manifest.webmanifest` | `https://dailygrind.example.com/manifest.webmanifest` | Replaces the old manifest; `migrate_to` prompts existing installs to migrate without visiting the new site first. Keep `id` identical to the old manifest's (`/`). Copy `/icons/` from the repo root alongside it. |
+| `move-notice.js` | `https://dailygrind.example.com/move-notice.js` | Banner for browsers that can't migrate automatically. |
+
+How it works (Chrome/Edge 149+):
+
+1. The new manifest (`/manifest.webmanifest` at the repo root) lists the old app's
+   id in `migrate_from`.
+2. The old origin confirms it with the `.well-known` file above.
+3. The browser offers to update the installed app. Its shortcuts, taskbar/dock pins,
+   and home screen icon now open the new origin, and the old installation is removed.
+
+To make the migration mandatory, add `"behavior": "force"` to the `migrate_from`
+entry in the new manifest. Users then have to update or remove the app.
+
+The two origins must stay same-site (same registrable domain, `example.com` here).
+Only the installation moves. Cookies, `localStorage`, IndexedDB, and permissions such
+as notifications stay with the old origin, so migrate those separately (for example
+server-side, keyed to the signed-in account) and ask for permissions again on the new origin.

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..8fc4c8f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/legacy-origin/move-notice.js
@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+// Fallback for browsers without Web App Origin Migration (Firefox, Safari,
+// older Chromium): tell users of the old installed app where it moved.
+// Include on every page of the old origin with <script src="/move-notice.js" defer></script>.
+(() => {
+  const NEW_ORIGIN = 'https://app.dailygrind.example.com';
+  const target = new URL(location.pathname + location.search + location.hash, NEW_ORIGIN);
+
+  const banner = document.createElement('aside');
+  banner.setAttribute('role', 'status');
+  banner.style.cssText =
+    'position:sticky;top:0;z-index:1001;padding:12px 5%;background:#ffab40;color:#3e2723;' +
+    'font:0.95rem/1.4 system-ui,sans-serif;text-align:center';
+
+  const installed = matchMedia('(display-mode: standalone)').matches;
+  banner.append(
+    installed
+      ? 'The Daily Grind app has moved. Install it from our new address, then remove this copy. '
+      : 'The Daily Grind has moved to a new address. '
+  );
+
+  const link = document.createElement('a');
+  link.href = target.href;
+  link.textContent = installed ? 'Open the new app' : 'Go to the new site';
+  link.style.cssText = 'color:inherit;font-weight:bold';
+  banner.append(link);
+
+  document.body.prepend(banner);
+})();
